newsitem.title: UK: Enron calls for modification to UK gas storage sale.
newsitem.headline: Enron calls for modification to UK gas storage sale.

text.p: UK gas pipeline operator Transco has received an urgent request from shipper Enron to reconsider the terms of its sale of storage gas, currently scheduled for July 1.

BG Plc unit Transco received an urgent modification proposal on Tuesday from Enron Capital and Trade Resources Limited, part of Enron Corp, asking that Transco be permitted to offer to sell gas in storage in tranches and at the National Balancing Point (NBP).

The pipeline operator had announced late last week it was to sell 5.38 terawatt hours (TWH) (around 180 million therms), with transfer to take place at Partington and at the offshore Rough storage facility on July 1.

Enron's proposed modification said that the Network Code, which governs transactions between Transco as pipeline operator and shippers as users, "currently requires Transco to sell off Residual Surplus Gas from System Margins and Top-up accounts through a Storage Transfer and on a single date. Bidding will be unnecessarily limited to shippers who hold sufficient storage capacity and the value of the gas will therefore not be maximised."

A Transco spokesman said that comments on the urgent modification are due to be received by Transco by 24 June, and they will be passed on to industry regulator Ofgas on 26 June. Ofgas will then reach a decision on 27 June.
The immediate effect is to quieten down market speculation on the consequence of the tender, which will now be delayed and may run for several months instead of on a single day.
